title: Note: reading a ghost story, part 4
summary: A short ghost story to read with the tools from earlier lessons: clauses with と, receptive verbs, たら chains, hearsay and てほしい.

blocks.text: This note is practice, not new grammar. Read the story one sentence at a time and break each sentence into clauses before you look for the meaning. So far: Mika lives in an old apartment. Every night at two o'clock she hears footsteps in the empty room upstairs.

The first sentence uses a **と** that links two clauses: when she went up, the door was open. The next two use receptive verbs (並べられていた, 閉められており) that say what was done to the dolls and the window, without saying who did it.

blocks.jp: 次の日の朝、みかが二階の部屋に行くと、ドアが少し開いていた。
blocks.en: The next morning, when Mika went up to the room on the second floor, the door was a little open.

blocks.jp: 部屋は暗くて、古い人形が床に並べられていた。
blocks.en: The room was dark, and old dolls had been lined up on the floor.

blocks.jp: 窓は閉められており、空気は冷たかった。
blocks.en: The window was shut and the air was cold.

blocks.text: 閉められており is a written way of joining clauses. It means the same as 閉められていて, only more formal. You will see it in stories and news.
A written join: 閉められ + ており, then the next clause.
Mika asks the landlord about the room. The next sentences are hearsay: **という** says that someone told her.

blocks.jp: 大家さんの話では、昔ここに住んでいた女の子が消えたという。
blocks.en: According to the landlord, a girl who used to live here disappeared.

blocks.jp: その子はまだこの家にいるかもしれないという。
blocks.en: They say she may still be in this house.

blocks.text: There is a small paper next to the dolls. 誰かに見つけてほしかった: the person you want to do it takes に, just like in 〜てもらう. Then comes a chain of 〜たら thoughts that ends in のに: "if I had not done it, it wouldn't have happened".

blocks.jp: 紙には「誰かに見つけてほしかった」と書いてあった。
blocks.en: The paper said, "I wanted someone to find me."

blocks.jp: あの時、二階に行かなかったら、こんなことにならなかったのに。
blocks.en: If I hadn't gone upstairs back then, it wouldn't have come to this.

blocks.jp: その夜、みかの部屋の前で、小さな足音が止まった。
blocks.en: That night, small footsteps stopped in front of Mika's room.

rows: と links two clauses: when she went
並べられていた / 閉められており
receptive: what was done, not who
誰かに見つけてほしい
if I hadn't... it wouldn't have

items: Break each sentence into clauses before you read the meaning.
Look for と clauses, receptive verbs and たら chains.
〜ており is a written way of saying 〜ていて.
Read the story again after the table: the second time, you should need far less help.
